headline: Learned models recover structure lost to sparsity and modality gaps in transcriptomics
label: Learned Spatial Transcriptomics Methods
summary: Recent spatial and single-cell papers apply graph, contrastive, and transformer learning to sparse, incomplete, or multi-omic transcriptomic measurements.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned representations that compensate for sparsity, partial measurement, or modality boundaries. In spatial transcriptomics, STORM applies low-rank tensor decomposition with spatial, histology and PPI priors to sparse data, DiSCO casts spot deconvolution as combinatorial optimization over a pretrained bipartite graph diffusion model, and DualCellChat reconstructs cell-cell interaction networks from incomplete measurements. Graph contrastive and autoencoder designs (GCAST, RGAST, STGAT, MLN2SVG, stCAMBL) target tissue domain identification, while PRESENT and GAMMI extend integration across modalities and samples. Single-cell work couples representation learning with biological priors, as in RegFormer and PVAED. New in this set are HEXST's hexagon-aware shifted-window attention for predicting spatial expression from H&E and FL-Sailer's federated scATAC-seq analysis with adaptive leverage score sampling.
